comments.content: The single-block case does not `break` after the last node when `first_node == last_node`, but the multi-block path computes `iovmax = min(IOV_MAX, c->conn->iovcnt)`. When there are more than `iovmax` blocks to write, the loop stops filling iov at `iovcnt < iovmax` without reaching `last_node`. In that case `total_bytes` only covers the first `iovmax` blocks — this is fine — but after a successful partial `writeToReplica`, subsequent calls rely on `postWriteToReplica` advancing `ref_repl_buf_node`. Please confirm the case where the number of blocks between `first_node` and `last_node` exceeds `iovmax`: the `if (cur_node == last_node) break;` is never hit, so writing stops early (correct), but ensure the client is rescheduled to write the remaining blocks rather than silently dropping data.

In the multi-block writev loop, when `connWritev` returns a partial write (`nwritten > 0` but `totwritten < total_bytes`), the outer `while (iovcnt > 0)` loops again and re-issues `connWritev` on the adjusted iov. For a non-blocking socket this will almost always return EAGAIN (<=0) on the second iteration, which then sets `WRITE_FLAGS_WRITE_ERROR` even though a partial write succeeded. This differs from the original code which returned after a short write without flagging an error. This can incorrectly mark the replica connection as errored. Consider breaking out of the loop on a successful partial write and letting the next event-loop iteration continue, rather than re-calling connWritev in a tight loop.

The write-offload guard now allows primary clients (previously `c->flag.primary` returned C_ERR). Only non-online replicas are excluded. Please verify that offloading writes for a `primary` client (i.e., we act as replica writing back to our primary, e.g. REPLCONF ACK) is actually safe with the new replica-specific write path, since `WRITE_FLAGS_IS_REPLICA` is only set when `getClientType(c) == CLIENT_TYPE_REPLICA`. A primary client would take the `_writeToClient` path here but its reply buffers may be handled elsewhere — confirm this is intended and tested.

`mock_connWritev` returns `int total` but accumulates into a `size_t total`; for large writes this truncates. More importantly, it never simulates a partial write (it always writes as much as fits in the buffer), so the retry-after-partial-write behavior in `writeToReplica` (the `while (iovcnt > 0)` loop) is not exercised by these tests. Consider adding a test that forces a short writev to cover the partial-write path.
